title: Environmental Impact of Fisheries
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 300L Environmental Impact of Fisheries curriculum: ecological effects of capture fishing (overfishing, bycatch, habitat destruction, ghost fishing), environmental effects of aquaculture (effluents, eutrophication, escapees, mangrove conversion), climate change impacts on fisheries, and environmental impact assessment (EIA) principles and mitigation. Kept distinct from Aquatic Pollution & Toxicology (FIS406), which focuses on pollutant chemistry/toxicology, and Sustainable Fisheries Management (FIS408), which focuses on broader sustainability theory and policy.

questions.question: Overfishing is best described, in an environmental-impact context, as:
options: Removing fish at a rate that exceeds the stock's capacity to replenish itself, degrading the resource over time
Any level of fishing activity, regardless of stock status
A situation where fish stocks are increasing faster than they are harvested
A term that applies only to aquaculture, never to capture fisheries
questions.correct_answer: Removing fish at a rate that exceeds the stock's capacity to replenish itself, degrading the resource over time
questions.explanation: Overfishing occurs when fishing mortality exceeds the rate at which a stock can reproduce and grow, leading to declining biomass and, potentially, long-term ecosystem impacts.

questions.question: Bottom trawling can have significant environmental impact mainly because it:
options: Physically disturbs and damages benthic (seabed) habitats and communities
Has no contact with the seabed at any point
Only affects fish found at the surface
Improves coral reef growth rates
questions.correct_answer: Physically disturbs and damages benthic (seabed) habitats and communities
questions.explanation: Trawl gear dragged along the seafloor can disrupt or destroy benthic habitats such as sponge and coral beds and disturb bottom-dwelling organisms, with long recovery times in some habitats.

questions.question: Bycatch, an environmental concern in many fisheries, refers to:
options: Non-target species incidentally caught and often discarded, sometimes including endangered species
The main species that a fishery intentionally targets
Fish that are voluntarily released before any capture occurs
Fish caught specifically for scientific tagging studies only
questions.correct_answer: Non-target species incidentally caught and often discarded, sometimes including endangered species
questions.explanation: Bycatch consists of unintended catches of non-target species, which may include juveniles of the target species, other commercial species, or vulnerable species like turtles and sharks, often discarded dead or dying.

questions.question: 'Ghost fishing' refers to the environmental problem in which:
options: Lost or abandoned fishing gear continues to entangle and kill marine life
Fish disappear entirely from a water body overnight
Fishers use supernatural methods to locate fish
A fishery is closed permanently by government decree
questions.correct_answer: Lost or abandoned fishing gear continues to entangle and kill marine life
questions.explanation: Ghost fishing occurs when lost, discarded, or abandoned nets, traps, and lines continue to passively catch and kill fish and other organisms long after being lost, wasting resources and harming ecosystems.

questions.question: The use of explosives (dynamite fishing) as an illegal fishing method causes environmental harm mainly by:
options: Indiscriminately killing marine organisms and destroying physical habitat such as reefs
Selectively harvesting only mature target fish with no other impact
Improving water clarity
Having effects limited only to the target species
questions.correct_answer: Indiscriminately killing marine organisms and destroying physical habitat such as reefs
questions.explanation: Blast fishing kills organisms of all sizes and species in the affected area indiscriminately and can physically shatter reef and other habitat structures, causing long-lasting ecological damage.

questions.question: Mangrove clearance for aquaculture pond construction is a significant environmental concern because mangroves:
options: Provide critical nursery habitat, coastal protection, and carbon storage that are lost when cleared
Have no ecological function of any kind
Only grow in freshwater rivers, unrelated to coastal fisheries
Regrow completely within days after clearance
questions.correct_answer: Provide critical nursery habitat, coastal protection, and carbon storage that are lost when cleared
questions.explanation: Mangroves serve as nursery grounds for many fish and shellfish species, buffer coastlines from erosion and storms, and store significant amounts of carbon, so their conversion to ponds represents a major ecological loss.

questions.question: Effluent discharge from intensive aquaculture ponds can cause eutrophication in receiving water bodies mainly because the effluent contains:
options: Elevated nutrients (nitrogen and phosphorus) from uneaten feed and fish waste
Only pure, nutrient-free water
Exclusively inert sand particles
Radioactive material
questions.correct_answer: Elevated nutrients (nitrogen and phosphorus) from uneaten feed and fish waste
questions.explanation: Aquaculture effluent is often enriched with nitrogen and phosphorus from feed residues and fish excretion; when discharged untreated it can trigger excessive algal growth (eutrophication) in receiving waters.

questions.question: Eutrophication resulting from nutrient enrichment of water bodies can ultimately lead to:
options: Algal blooms followed by oxygen depletion when the algae die and decompose
Permanently increased water clarity
A guaranteed increase in fish populations with no downside
Complete elimination of all nutrients from the system
questions.correct_answer: Algal blooms followed by oxygen depletion when the algae die and decompose
questions.explanation: Excess nutrients drive rapid algal growth; when the bloom dies, bacterial decomposition consumes large amounts of dissolved oxygen, potentially causing hypoxia and fish kills.

questions.question: The escape of farmed fish into the wild is an environmental concern mainly because escapees can:
options: Interbreed with, compete with, or spread disease to wild populations
Improve the genetic diversity of wild stocks in every case
Have zero interaction with wild fish
Automatically die immediately upon release
questions.correct_answer: Interbreed with, compete with, or spread disease to wild populations
questions.explanation: Escaped farmed fish, especially non-native or genetically distinct stocks, can interbreed with wild populations (altering genetic diversity), compete for resources, or introduce pathogens and parasites.

questions.question: The use of wild-caught fish (such as small pelagics) to produce fishmeal for aquaculture feed raises environmental concern mainly because it can:
options: Place additional fishing pressure on wild forage fish stocks that are also ecologically important
Have no relationship to wild fish populations
Guarantee the recovery of overfished stocks
Eliminate the need for any capture fisheries
questions.correct_answer: Place additional fishing pressure on wild forage fish stocks that are also ecologically important
questions.explanation: Fishmeal production relies on wild-caught forage fish, and high demand for aquafeed can add pressure on these stocks, which also play a key ecological role as prey for larger fish, seabirds, and marine mammals.

questions.question: Climate change is expected to affect fisheries resources mainly through:
options: Rising water temperatures, altered rainfall patterns, and shifting species distributions
Complete cessation of all water evaporation
Guaranteed increases in fish stocks everywhere
No measurable change to aquatic ecosystems
questions.correct_answer: Rising water temperatures, altered rainfall patterns, and shifting species distributions
questions.explanation: Climate change affects fisheries through warming waters, changing precipitation and river flow patterns, ocean acidification, and shifts in the geographic ranges of fish species.

questions.question: Ocean acidification, linked to rising atmospheric carbon dioxide, is a particular concern for marine fisheries because it can:
options: Impair shell and skeleton formation in shellfish and some plankton, disrupting marine food webs
Increase seawater pH to dangerously high levels
Have no effect on any marine organism
Only affect freshwater fish, not marine species
questions.correct_answer: Impair shell and skeleton formation in shellfish and some plankton, disrupting marine food webs
questions.explanation: As oceans absorb more CO2, seawater pH decreases (acidification), which impairs calcification in shellfish, corals, and calcifying plankton, potentially disrupting marine food webs that fisheries depend on.

questions.question: Reduced river flow and shrinking of Lake Chad over recent decades illustrate how environmental change can affect Nigerian inland fisheries by:
options: Diminishing the water habitat available to sustain fish populations and fisher livelihoods
Having no bearing on inland fishery productivity
Guaranteeing an increase in fish catches
Only affecting marine, not inland, fisheries
questions.correct_answer: Diminishing the water habitat available to sustain fish populations and fisher livelihoods
questions.explanation: The well-documented shrinkage of Lake Chad, driven by climatic and hydrological changes, has reduced available fish habitat and negatively affected the livelihoods of fishing communities dependent on the lake.

questions.question: An Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) conducted before establishing a large aquaculture facility is intended to:
options: Systematically identify and evaluate the likely environmental effects of the project before it proceeds
Replace the need for any government approval
Guarantee that the project will have zero environmental impact
Only assess the project's financial profitability
questions.correct_answer: Systematically identify and evaluate the likely environmental effects of the project before it proceeds
questions.explanation: EIA is a formal, structured process for predicting and evaluating the environmental consequences of a proposed development, informing decision-making and mitigation planning before implementation.

questions.question: Mitigation measures in an EIA process, once potential negative impacts are identified, are intended to:
options: Avoid, reduce, or compensate for the predicted adverse environmental effects
Increase the severity of environmental harm
Eliminate the need for any monitoring after project approval
Apply only after the entire project is completed
questions.correct_answer: Avoid, reduce, or compensate for the predicted adverse environmental effects
questions.explanation: Mitigation measures are actions built into project design and operation to avoid, minimize, or offset adverse environmental impacts identified during the EIA process.

questions.question: Habitat destruction from coastal or riverbank aquaculture development is often assessed in an EIA by examining impacts on:
options: Wetlands, mangroves, or other critical natural habitats near the project site
Only the internal pond water chemistry
The market price of fish feed
Global stock exchange indices
questions.correct_answer: Wetlands, mangroves, or other critical natural habitats near the project site
questions.explanation: EIA studies for coastal or riverine aquaculture projects evaluate potential losses or alteration of nearby sensitive habitats such as wetlands and mangroves, which provide important ecological services.

questions.question: Discharge of untreated aquaculture pond sludge into natural waterways is a concern mainly because the sludge:
options: Contains concentrated organic matter and nutrients that can deplete oxygen and alter benthic communities downstream
Is entirely inert and has no chemical or biological content
Improves the water quality of the receiving stream
Cannot be transported by water at all
questions.correct_answer: Contains concentrated organic matter and nutrients that can deplete oxygen and alter benthic communities downstream
questions.explanation: Pond sludge accumulates organic waste, uneaten feed residues, and nutrients; if discharged untreated it can cause oxygen depletion and ecological disruption in the receiving water body.

questions.question: The introduction of non-native (exotic) fish species for aquaculture carries environmental risk mainly because such species may:
options: Become invasive, outcompeting or preying upon native species if they escape into the wild
Always fail to survive outside captivity
Have no ecological interaction with native fauna under any circumstances
Automatically improve native biodiversity
questions.correct_answer: Become invasive, outcompeting or preying upon native species if they escape into the wild
questions.explanation: Non-native species introduced for farming can become invasive if they escape and establish wild populations, potentially outcompeting, preying on, or hybridizing with native species and disrupting ecosystems.

questions.question: Destructive fishing gears such as very fine-mesh nets contribute to environmental degradation of fisheries mainly by:
options: Capturing large numbers of juvenile fish before they can reproduce, undermining stock recruitment
Selectively catching only old, post-reproductive fish
Having no effect on fish population age structure
Improving the survival rate of juvenile fish
questions.correct_answer: Capturing large numbers of juvenile fish before they can reproduce, undermining stock recruitment
questions.explanation: Fine-mesh or undersized gear captures immature fish before they reach reproductive age, reducing the stock's capacity to replenish itself through natural recruitment.

questions.question: Which of the following best illustrates a cumulative environmental impact in fisheries?
options: Many small-scale pollution and habitat disturbances from multiple sources combining to produce a larger overall ecological effect over time
A single, isolated, one-time event with no lasting consequence
An impact that occurs and then disappears instantly with no trace
An effect that is always immediately reversed by natural processes
questions.correct_answer: Many small-scale pollution and habitat disturbances from multiple sources combining to produce a larger overall ecological effect over time
questions.explanation: Cumulative impacts arise when the combined effect of multiple, individually modest stressors (e.g., several fish farms, land-use changes) accumulates to a level of ecological significance greater than any single source alone.

questions.question: A marine protected area (MPA) is used as an environmental management tool in fisheries mainly to:
options: Provide a refuge where fish stocks and habitats can recover with limited or no extractive activity
Increase fishing pressure within its boundaries
Serve exclusively as a tourist attraction with no ecological role
Replace the need for any other fisheries management measure
questions.correct_answer: Provide a refuge where fish stocks and habitats can recover with limited or no extractive activity
questions.explanation: MPAs restrict or exclude fishing and other extractive activities within designated areas, allowing habitats and fish populations to recover and potentially spill over into adjacent fished areas.

questions.question: Antibiotic and chemical residues from intensive aquaculture operations pose an environmental concern mainly because they can:
options: Persist in the environment and contribute to antimicrobial resistance in bacteria
Immediately and completely biodegrade with zero ecological trace
Improve water clarity permanently
Have no interaction with surrounding aquatic organisms
questions.correct_answer: Persist in the environment and contribute to antimicrobial resistance in bacteria
questions.explanation: Residues from antibiotics and other chemicals used in aquaculture can persist in sediments and water, potentially promoting the development of antimicrobial-resistant bacteria in the wider environment.

questions.question: Sand and gravel dredging in rivers, often done for construction material, affects fisheries mainly by:
options: Destroying spawning substrates and increasing turbidity that harms fish habitat
Having no relationship to fish habitat
Automatically improving spawning success
Reducing river water flow to zero permanently
questions.correct_answer: Destroying spawning substrates and increasing turbidity that harms fish habitat
questions.explanation: Dredging disturbs riverbed substrates important for spawning and increases suspended sediment (turbidity), both of which can degrade fish habitat quality and reproductive success.

questions.question: A key principle of the precautionary approach in fisheries environmental management is that:
options: Lack of full scientific certainty should not be used as a reason to postpone measures to prevent environmental harm
Management action should only occur after damage has already become irreversible
Scientific uncertainty means no management measures are ever justified
Precaution applies only to aquaculture and never to capture fisheries
questions.correct_answer: Lack of full scientific certainty should not be used as a reason to postpone measures to prevent environmental harm
questions.explanation: The precautionary approach holds that management should act to prevent potential serious or irreversible environmental harm even before complete scientific certainty is achieved.

questions.question: Post-harvest fish waste (offal, processing byproducts) discharged untreated into waterways can cause environmental harm mainly through:
options: Organic pollution leading to oxygen depletion and foul odor in receiving waters
Immediate improvement of water clarity
Increasing the dissolved oxygen content dramatically
Having no measurable biological or chemical effect
questions.correct_answer: Organic pollution leading to oxygen depletion and foul odor in receiving waters
questions.explanation: Untreated fish processing waste is high in organic matter; its decomposition in receiving waters consumes dissolved oxygen and can cause unpleasant odors and localized ecological stress.

questions.question: Monitoring programs established after a fisheries or aquaculture project begins operating are important because they:
options: Track actual environmental impacts over time and verify whether mitigation measures are working
Are legally required only before project approval, never afterward
Have no role once the EIA has been approved
Replace the need for the original EIA study
questions.correct_answer: Track actual environmental impacts over time and verify whether mitigation measures are working
questions.explanation: Post-approval monitoring allows managers to compare predicted impacts against actual outcomes, assess the effectiveness of mitigation measures, and adjust management as needed.

questions.question: Reduction of biodiversity due to selective removal of top predator fish species from an ecosystem is an example of:
options: A trophic cascade effect altering the balance of the food web
An impact limited strictly to the removed species with no wider consequence
A guaranteed increase in overall ecosystem stability
An effect that only occurs in freshwater systems, never marine
questions.correct_answer: A trophic cascade effect altering the balance of the food web
questions.explanation: Removing top predators can trigger a trophic cascade, releasing prey populations from predation pressure and altering the structure and balance of the wider food web.

questions.question: Sedimentation caused by land clearing and erosion upstream of a fishery can degrade aquatic habitat mainly by:
options: Smothering benthic habitat and reducing light penetration needed for primary production
Adding beneficial nutrients with no negative consequences
Increasing water clarity for fish feeding
Having no measurable relationship to fish habitat quality
questions.correct_answer: Smothering benthic habitat and reducing light penetration needed for primary production
questions.explanation: Excess sediment from erosion can bury benthic organisms and spawning substrate and reduce light penetration necessary for aquatic plant and algal photosynthesis, degrading overall habitat quality.

questions.question: Stakeholder consultation with local fishing communities during an EIA for a proposed fisheries or aquaculture project is important mainly because it:
options: Incorporates local ecological knowledge and social concerns that might otherwise be overlooked in the assessment
Is a purely symbolic step with no bearing on the final EIA decision
Replaces the need for any scientific environmental data
Is required only for projects with no environmental impact at all
questions.correct_answer: Incorporates local ecological knowledge and social concerns that might otherwise be overlooked in the assessment
questions.explanation: Local communities often hold valuable knowledge of local ecology and depend directly on the resource, so genuine consultation improves the accuracy and social legitimacy of the EIA process.
